newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges up on demand, short covering.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges up on demand, short covering.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges closed a little higher on Thursday, breaking through the week's top range, with traders citing good demand to cover short positions and tight cargoes as the forces behind the move to the upside.
High sulphur cargoes were assessed steady in the $84/$85 cif region after swaps gained a little from Wednesday and one percent was also stable with some buying interest seen.

High sulphur fuel barges traded at $86.25 and $86.50 fob ARA, or 50 cents over the highest number achieved earlier this week, after earlier trades at 50 cent intervals from $84.50 to $86. These compared with Wednesday's range of $84/$85.25.
A major that bought at $85.50 and $86 said it did so as there was a shortness of material coupled with high bunker demand, in excess of 20,000 tonnes, and was considering to do $87.
Another trader said the rise was attributed to the sudden absence of sellers from the market, with three players only seen late in the day.

"People are seeing that cargoes are getting tighter and tighter and the market is rising. If demand continues then people will be short...I am even considering to buy at $87," a trader with the major said.
A third trader said: "There has been some demand and some people were aggressive on the selling side earlier this week in bunkers and now have to cover short positions. That's why it is going up."

Low sulphur fuel barges were inactive with talk largely steady to a little weaker on the offer side at $96.50, while the few buyers out there were heard to have cut their bids to $94. Others were at $95.
"The numbers moved a little lower with lack of deals out there. There doesn't seem to be that much buying interest at the moment," one trader said.
Two lower quality high sulphur cracked cargoes were still steady, offered in the $82 cif range but buyers, knowing the cargoes were distressed, were up to $3 lower, traders said.
One percent was largely steady talked in the $92.50/$93.50 fob area after trades around the lower figure over the past few days.
At least three sellers were heard actively offering, with $93 fob seen as the mark for any possible deals, and an Italian buyer was heard still looking on the market.
A large parcel of 70,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel was bought up on Wednesday at high fob +$f2.50, traders said, and was going into the Mediterranean.
